concept.title: Visual Editor
concept.shortdesc: Edit a DITA topic on a page that looks like your output, while DITA Craft writes clean XML: every change reaches the file as a small, precise text edit, and everything you do not touch stays exactly as it was.

section.title: Overview
section.p: The visual editor shows a topic as a page — headings, paragraphs, notes, steps, lists, tables, figures — and lets you edit it right there. It is built from the same grammars as the visual preview, so the page follows your document type: the styles, menus and the Enter key only offer what the DTD allows at the cursor, and specialized elements behave like the element they specialize.

The visual editor is an alternative editor for .dita, .ditamap and .bookmap files: the text editor stays the default, and both edit the same document. Open a topic or a map with DITA: Open in Visual Editor.

ul.li: Write on the page: paragraphs, lists, steps, styles and any element your DTD allows, from the keyboard, the toolbar or the right-click menu.
Edit CALS and simple tables, and drag column borders to set widths.
Insert, paste, drop and resize images; link to elements, keys, topics and web addresses from a picker.
See reused content, keys' texts and link titles resolved; open the source of reused content or make a local copy.
See the language server's problems on the page and apply their quick fixes.
Work on maps and bookmaps: one row per reference with the title of its topic, folded and opened from the page.
Edit attributes in the Properties view, and work side by side with the XML.
